taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce nutans is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Upright to ascending annual spurge with relatively large opposite leaves, often marked with a reddish blotch, and loose branching rather than a flat mat.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew treats Chamaesyce nutans as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia nutans.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae/Euphorbia: milky latex and highly reduced flowers grouped into a cyathium; in sandmat spurges, opposite leaves, stem habit, hairiness, and capsule traits are especially useful.
best_field_traits: leaves often show reddish central blotch
larger and more upright than most sandmats
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The easiest split is habit: E. nutans rises off the ground and has much larger leaves than E. serpens or E. prostrata.
